title: When the Hollow Burns Revisited
premise: August Amberdale, the king's food-taster, has survived three years of outlawed magic by keeping their hedge-witch charms small and their head down. When a dying courier presses a map to the Hollow—a buried covenant-stone binding the human city to the fae realm of Emberfall—August learns the covenant is failing, and the unnatural winter descending on the city is the fae's dying breath. Hunted by the Lord Chancellor's witch-finders and shadowed by Wren, the courier's vengeful daughter, August must gather the scattered oath-kin named on the map and reforge the covenant at the Hollow. In the climax, August offers their own carefully cultivated poison-immunity as the covenant's new anchor—swallowing the realm's grief so both peoples can survive—ending the winter but binding them forever as the living bridge between realms, no longer invisible, finally belonging to something larger than themselves.
about_author: Silas Okafor is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade working palace-adjacent banquets before turning to fiction, and whose stories braid food, folklore, and quiet acts of rebellion. They write from a kitchen table crowded with herb pots and half-finished maps.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: August's POV. A morning of tasting the king's breakfast, cataloging poisons by aftertaste, then slipping to the night market to sell a luck-charm to a baker's widow. We learn magic is punishable by burning, and August's charms are small enough to pass as superstition. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a life built on small, deniable kindnesses.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: August's POV. A bloodied stranger collapses against August's tenement door, pressing an oilskin map into their hands and gasping that the Hollow is waking. Witch-finders' boots echo in the stairwell; the stranger dies holding August's wrist. Emotional beat: terror and unwilling complicity—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Say
chapters.summary: August's POV, with a brief Wren interlude. August deciphers the map's covenant-script by candlelight while deciding whether to burn it; the script only reveals itself to oath-blood, which August apparently carries. Wren, watching from the rooftops, believes August stole her father's map. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the first thrill of inheritance.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The courier's daughter confronts August with a knife and a grievance; they fight, then call a wary truce when witch-finders raid the block. Wren reveals her father spent years searching for the Hollow to end the winter killing Emberfall's children. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into alliance.

chapters.title: The First Name
chapters.summary: August's POV. The map's first name leads to Mother Hesk, a disgraced royal physician hiding in a leper hospice, who explains the covenant: a stone where human and fae oaths were exchanged, now cracked. Hesk agrees to help but warns the Chancellor already hunts the map's bearers. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Garden
chapters.summary: August's POV. Summoned to taste at a state banquet, August must serve the Lord Chancellor—the man who outlawed magic—while reading the room for signs the hunt is closing in. A poisoned dish meant for the Chancellor nearly kills August; their immunity saves them but exposes something inhuman in their blood. Emotional beat: the taster becomes the tasted.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The witch-finders burn a charm-seller alive in the market square as a message. Wren and August realize the crackdown is orchestrated by Chancellor Veyre, who knows the covenant is failing and intends to let the fae die rather than share the city. Emotional beat: mourning hardened into purpose.

chapters.title: The River Oath
chapters.summary: August's POV. The second name on the map is a river-warden, Tam, half-fae and passing as human, who guards a submerged fragment of the old oath-stone. Tam tests August with a drowning rite; August survives by tasting the water's grief. Emotional beat: the cost of belonging—nothing on this road is free.

chapters.title: Long Winter Falling
chapters.summary: August's POV. Frost kills the palace gardens in midsummer; the king sickens with a wasting no physician can name. August realizes the realm itself is dying with the covenant, and the Chancellor is blaming magic for a wound magic alone can heal. Emotional beat: the stakes turn from personal to civilizational.

chapters.title: The Hollow's Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the map's spine, the trio reaches the hills above the city and finds the Hollow's entrance sealed by a riddle of tastes and scents only an oath-kin can solve. August opens it; inside, the covenant-stone lies split down its heart. Emotional beat: awe and vertigo at the scale of what's been broken.

chapters.title: What Emberfall Remembers
chapters.summary: August's POV. Below the Hollow lies Emberfall's threshold, where the fae's memories pool like wine. August drinks and sees the original covenant: two peoples, one oath, and the first betrayal—a human king who hoarded the stone's power. Emotional beat: inherited guilt, and the understanding that the map chose them for a reason.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Heir
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Tam reveals the map's final name is Veyre's own—the Chancellor is descended from the betraying king and has been draining the stone for decades to extend his life. Wren wants vengeance; August argues the covenant, not the man, must come first. Emotional beat: the alliance strains over justice versus survival.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: August's POV. Witch-finders ambush the group on the descent; Hesk is captured buying their escape, and Tam is gravely wounded. August must choose between rescuing Hesk and reaching the stone before the solstice eclipse, when the covenant can still be reforged. Emotional beat: the arithmetic of sacrifice, and its bitterness.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Bargain
chapters.summary: August's POV, in captivity. Veyre offers August a deal: the map and freedom in exchange for opening the Hollow, which only oath-blood can do. He shows August the dying fae realm through a scrying glass—children of light guttering like candles. Emotional beat: temptation, and August's refusal to let compassion be weaponized.

chapters.title: The Kitchen War
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, Tam, and the hospice faithful mount a rescue, using August's knowledge of the palace kitchens—poison, allergens, and service corridors—to breach the Chancellor's wing. August escapes mid-execution when their own immunity turns the executioner's toxins harmless. Emotional beat: the small skills of the invisible become weapons of the seen.

chapters.title: Flight to the Hollow
chapters.summary: August's POV. A desperate race through blizzard-wrapped hills, pursued by Veyre's riders. Hesk, freed but failing, gives August her physician's knowledge of the oath-rites and her blessing. Emotional beat: found family forged under fire; grief carried forward instead of left behind.

chapters.title: The Eclipse Opens
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach the Hollow as the eclipse begins; Veyre arrives with his guard, and the two claimants of the betraying bloodline face each other across the split stone. The fae realm flickers visibly in the sky above the hills. Emotional beat: everything converges; no more hiding places.

chapters.title: The Hollow Burns
chapters.summary: August's POV. Veyre tries to seize the stone's power and is consumed by it—inheritance without obligation. The covenant demands a new anchor: not a king, but someone who has spent years taking poison in small doses for others. August understands, and steps forward. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into choice.

chapters.title: One Dish at a Time
chapters.summary: August's POV. The reforging: August swallows the realm's grief as they once swallowed poison, dish by dish, taste by taste, until the stone seals around their heartbeat. The winter breaks over the hills. Emotional beat: the climax's cost made intimate—salvation as an act of sustained, deliberate endurance.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The city wakes to green; fae light returns to the river; the new king repeals the magic laws. Wren buries her father's map at the Hollow's mouth, his work finished. August survives, changed—able to taste both realms in every bite. Emotional beat: mourning braided with relief.

chapters.title: The Taster's Table
chapters.summary: August's POV. August declines a court title and opens a small supper house at the Hollow's foot, where human and fae eat side by side and every dish carries a trace of both realms. Wren runs the door; Tam tends the river. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: What the Stone Keeps
chapters.summary: August's POV, coda. On the first anniversary, August visits the sealed stone and feels its second heartbeat answer their own. A new stranger arrives with a question and a map of her own, and August—no longer invisible, no longer alone—opens the door. Emotional beat: the cycle continues, but this time with open hands.
